paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: : Loss steps
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the training loss over iterations for five different model configurations, comparing their convergence behavior. The x-axis, labeled "#Iteration", spans from 0 to 140,000 iterations with a linear scale and tick marks at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis, labeled "Loss", ranges from 2.4 to 3.4 with a linear scale and tick marks at intervals of 0.1. The plot contains five distinct lines: the "Vanilla" model is represented by a purple line with circular markers; "StrmLLM (n=64)" is a blue line with circular markers; "SepLLM (n=64)" is an orange line with circular markers; "SepLLM (n=64, H)" is a green line with circular markers; and "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)" is a red line with circular markers. The final line, "SepLLM (n=128)", is a dark blue line with circular markers. All lines begin at a high loss value near 3.4 at iteration 0 and exhibit a rapid initial decline, followed by a slower, more gradual decrease toward a stable minimum loss value around 2.5 after approximately 60,000 iterations. The "Vanilla" model shows the most rapid initial drop, reaching a loss of approximately 2.6 at 20,000 iterations and stabilizing near 2.5. The "StrmLLM (n=64)" model follows closely, reaching a loss of approximately 2.7 at 20,000 iterations and stabilizing near 2.6. The "SepLLM" variants generally converge to a slightly lower loss than "StrmLLM" and "Vanilla" by the end of the training period, with "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)" and "SepLLM (n=128)" stabilizing near 2.5. The "SepLLM (n=128)" model shows the slowest initial convergence but reaches a similar final loss value as the other models.
